slides.0.title: Industry and markets
slides.0.subtitle: Export structure and price tiers
slides.1.title: Export structure (2024)
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Volume and value
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Exports in 2024 were 64.2 million litres (−1.7%) and EUR 233.3 million (−6.0%) (provisional Statistik Austria data)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Germany
slides.1.highlights.1.content: 60.2% of volume and 42.3% of value: large in volume but lower in unit price
slides.1.highlights.2.title: USA
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The USA took 8.5% of 2024 export value and moved into second place, while Switzerland fell sharply
slides.1.highlights.3.title: Bulk wine
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Bulk exports rose 16.1% in volume in 2024 but fell 1.4% in value
slides.1.content: The year matters: 2025 data show 60.6 million litres and about EUR 219 million (see Level 1), a trend of steady volume and falling value.
slides.2.title: Structural risks and opportunities
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Dependence on Germany
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Concentration in one market exposes the industry directly to price and demand swings
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Sustainability as differentiation
slides.2.highlights.1.content: About 27% of vineyards are Sustainable Austria certified (see L3-1), organic about 25% (preliminary, November 2024)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Branding via whites and DACs
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Building recognition through Grüner Veltliner and DAC region names is central to the export story (a descriptive judgement)
slides.2.content: No figures are given for producer types and price tiers: no reliable official statistics were obtained, to avoid misleading.
slides.3.title: Diploma depth: producer structure and routes to market
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Small estates and direct sales
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Austria is dominated by small family estates; the Heuriger (Vienna, Lower Austria) and Buschenschank (Styria) let estates sell wine and food on site at high margins and build a local following. A pine branch (Buschen) over the door traditionally shows they are open
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Co-operatives and large firms
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Co-operatives matter in some regions, such as Domäne Wachau in the Wachau and Winzer Krems in Kremstal; large firms such as Lenz Moser and Sekt houses such as Schlumberger handle volume retail and export (representative examples, not a full list)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Reading “stable volume, falling value”
slides.3.highlights.2.content: In 2024 Germany took about 60% of export volume but only about 40% of value, and bulk volume rose while its value fell, signalling a growing share of cheap bulk. Possible responses: more bottled, DAC and Ried wines and growth in higher-value markets such as the US (course judgement, not an official conclusion)
slides.3.highlights.3.title: Positioning language for essays
slides.3.highlights.3.content: Austria’s export story centres on three points: dry whites (Grüner) + regional style (DAC) + sustainability; its weaknesses are small volume, high cost and dependence on one market. In essays, acknowledge the scale limits first, then discuss the premium strategy
slides.3.content: A small, high-cost producer can only take the road of quality and recognisability.
Roughly what share of Austria's wine export volume did Germany take in 2024?
Germany took 60.2% of volume and 42.3% of value.
Which market became the second-largest export market by value in 2024?
The USA took 8.5% and moved to second.
B. Large volume but relatively low unit price
60.2% of volume against 42.3% of value implies a lower unit price.
